findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: After a caller invokes the returned disposer, subsequent `message` events still reach the supposedly detached handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also retain closures and invoke stale handlers multiple times. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` to preserve the existing cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
For any socket that emits a `"message"` after the returned cleanup function is called, the handler still executes. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate stale listeners, causing duplicate processing and leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
Any caller that invokes the returned disposer expects the registered `"message"` handler to be detached. The new no-op leaves it active, so subsequent messages still invoke disposed handlers, causing duplicate/stale processing and unbounded listener accumulation across repeated attach/cleanup cycles.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore message-listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, the socket still delivers attacker-controlled messages to the stale handler. In environments using disposal for logout, authorization revocation, tenant changes, or component teardown, the handler can continue operating with obsolete privileged state and accumulate indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
After callers invoke the disposer, the `"message"` listener remains attached. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate retained handler closures and invoke every stale handler for each message, causing unbounded memory and processing growth on long-lived sockets.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
